ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND to have placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The record shows the call limb only — a single in-app call at 11:14:20 that was not answered and rang 20 s (EV-TRIP-05065) — and no chat message from the driver at all: the chat log's one and only entry is the rider's own message at 11:06:00, and the platform's own derived contact_before_cancel block returns message_count 0, complete false and obligation_met false (EV-CHAT-05065). I rely on EV-CHAT-05065 as impaired evidence: TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6, 1 of 3 entries exported with nothing after 11:06:00. On the record as it stands the message limb of the contact obligation fails, and POL-NS-23 is express that the fee is then voided 'with no driver compensation' — so the driver cannot recover the 5.00 under POL-NS-22 even though he cancelled 380 s after arriving.

The driver's claim says he 'sent message and called', but the trip record's own event log shows what actually happened at that pickup: a platform push notification at 11:11:54 ('Your driver has arrived') and one in-app call at 11:14:20 that was not answered (EV-TRIP-05065). A system push is not an in-app chat message, and an unanswered call is not a message; POL-NS-23 requires both limbs, each before the cancellation, and nothing in this record supplies the message limb. The chat log I rely on for that is impaired — TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 (EV-CHAT-05065).

If the judge reads the truncated chat export as leaving the message limb unproved rather than disproved, the rider still wins the money point: whether the driver messaged before cancelling is a fact POL-NS-23 needs, and the only evidence that would carry it is impaired — the export holds 1 entry against trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 and covers nothing after 11:06:00, so the arrival and the whole waiting window are absent (EV-CHAT-05065, weight_multiplier 0.6, TRUNCATED_LOG; EV-TRIP-05065). POL-GEN-26 names this very fact ('whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling') and requires escalation. ESCALATE is terminal, issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the 5.00 already refunded to the rider is not restored to the driver and no fee is collected from the rider. POL-NS-26 expressly subjects even a final no-show ruling to POL-GEN-26.

I do not contest the wait, and I say so plainly: POL-NS-21's free wait runs 300 s from the driver's arrival, the record puts arrival at 11:11:50 and cancellation at 11:18:10 — 380 s — and the GPS trace corroborates the arrival, the nearest fix sitting 2.05 m from the pickup at 11:12:30 with 5.0 m reported accuracy, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (EV-GPS-05065; EV-TRIP-05065). That discharges POL-NS-21 and it does nothing for POL-NS-23, which is a separate and cumulative contact obligation the driver must also satisfy before he may cancel for no-show.

The filer here is the driver (dispute.filed_by = DRIVER) and the disputed 5.00 is already off the rider: the ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 against total_charged 5.00 (EV-FARE-05065), and the trip record records the fee_reversed event at 13:59:10 — 5.00 refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (EV-TRIP-05065). What the driver seeks is restoration of that 5.00 to himself. POL-GEN-03 defines FULL_REFUND against the filing party, so on a driver's filing FULL_REFUND would run to the driver; it is not the rider's remedy and the rider does not ask for it. The rider's entitlement is that the disputed charge is not collected, which is exactly what the present state already achieves: NO_ACTION — the filing party's claim not supported, both amount fields null and no driver compensation.

No POL-NS-25 repeat-no-show referral is available on this profile. ledger.claim: The driver's arrival at the pickup is established on clean evidence: the trip record's driver_arrived event at 11:11:50 is corroborated by the driver's GPS trace under POL-NS-21, whose nearest fix to the pickup point is 2.05 m away with a reported accuracy of 5 m — well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — and the arrival check returns corroborated true.

The driver served the free wait in fact, not merely on paper: the driver's trace carries thirteen consecutive zero-speed fixes holding position at the pickup from 11:11:30 through 11:18:00, and the platform recorded wait_timer_expired at 11:16:55 with the rider not on board, so the 300 s POL-NS-21 requires was actually waited.

The cancellation came after the free wait: POL-NS-21's clock starts from the driver's arrival (11:11:50) so the 300 s free wait expired at 11:16:50, while the driver cancelled at 11:18:10 — 380 s after arrival — which satisfies POL-NS-22's precondition of a cancellation after the free wait.

The call limb of POL-NS-23 is satisfied on the clean record: the trip record's in_app_calls carries one call placed by the driver at 11:14:20, unanswered after ringing 20 s, which is before cancelled_at (11:18:10) and is exactly the trip_record.in_app_calls entry the clause names.

The message limb is not shown to be missing. The chat log is IMPAIRED — issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight multiplier 0.6 — because the export holds only 1 entry (11:06:00) while trip_record.chat_message_count is 3, and the absent entries cover the arrival and the entire waiting window. POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the driver's message 'is missing', and the absence of a message from a truncated export does not establish that no message was ever sent.

The counterparty statement does not fill that gap: the rider concedes the call ('Only a missed call') and asserts only that he received no arrival message, and a party's recollection of what he did or did not receive cannot establish what the platform's own chat system carried before the cancellation.

With the arrival, the free wait and the call all carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, the fee is not voided and the ledger's own arithmetic compels the driver's outcome: the fare breakdown charges 5.00 SGD, the policy fee is 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy is true, so POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

No confidence floor bars that ruling: the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and the only profile field POL-GEN-22 makes relevant is fraud_flags, which is 0 on both profiles, so neither the 0.80 nor the 0.95 threshold applies, and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final. The chat log's 0.6 weight caps confidence in anything drawn from it alone; it sets no floor below which this trip must go to a human.

NO_ACTION would be wrong here: the present state (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, the fee already recovered from the driver) leaves the driver 5.00 SGD out of pocket, and POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION preserves that state rather than restoring the charge.

ruling.explanation:
The events up to the wait are not in dispute and the record confirms them. The driver arrived at the pickup at 11:11:50 — the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup with 5 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (POL-NS-21). The 300-second free wait therefore ran from 11:11:50 to 11:16:50, and the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 380 seconds after arrival. That much of the driver's case is accepted: the wait was served and the fee is not void for want of waiting.

The case turns on the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23, which requires BOTH an in-app chat message AND an in-app call before cancelling. The call limb is met on clean evidence: one in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered after 20 s, before the 11:18:10 cancellation (EV-TRIP-05065). The message limb cannot be decided either way. The chat export (EV-CHAT-05065) is impaired — TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6 — holding only 1 of the 3 messages the trip record counts (chat_message_count 3), with nothing after 11:06:00, so the arrival and the entire waiting window are absent. That is exactly the stretch where a driver's pre-cancellation message would sit. An impaired limb is undecided, and POL-GEN-26 names this very fact — 'whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling' — as one that, where the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired, escalates the case instead of deciding it; POL-NS-26 subjects even the final no-show ruling to POL-GEN-26.

So the driver's request to have the 5.00 SGD restored (POL-NS-22: DRIVER_COMPENSATION, both amount fields 5.00) is rejected — it needs the message limb to hold, and an undecided limb cannot support restoring the fee. The driver is right that a truncated export does not prove a message was never sent, but it does not prove one was sent either, so that point does not carry the fee. The rider's contrary argument — that the fee is voided because the message limb is missing — goes equally too far: the message is unproven, not proven absent, so POL-NS-23's FULL_REFUND trigger is not established and the rider cannot be declared the winner on it. The rider's submission that the present state should simply stand as NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 is rejected too: escalation holds the amount rather than leaving a money outcome in place.

Confidence is capped at 0.6, the weight of the impaired chat log that carries the undecided fact (POL-GEN-02(2)); the required bar here is POL-NS-26's, and the 5.00 SGD disputed value sits below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band with fraud_flags 0 on both profiles, so no higher bar applies. No referral is produced: the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, so POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag cannot be computed, and the 5.00 SGD charged matches the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire. The open question for the human reviewer is whether the driver sent an in-app chat message before cancelling; the 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver is held as it stands, neither collected nor refunded further, pending that review.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
